links.note: Yes/No grid on a set of animals: they all lay eggs (reproduction) and they all respond to stimuli - both are 32768's content. Not 32765, which is the living/non-living sort itself rather than the named characteristics.

Activity 10.4 verbatim: the three-month bean-plant table, flower parts developing into a pod, and the plant drying after seeds form. 32773 is the only concept holding the plant life cycle; 32769 is the germination pots.
Activity 10.2's own table - four pots A-D differing in one condition each. 32769 is that design; 32770 is only the per-seed light rule.
Activity 10.3's table: three beakers, upright/inverted/one-direction light, predictions then observations for shoot and root.
The shell may be the home and part of a living snail - deciding whether a thing in front of you is living. That is 32765's test-building, not 32768's list of characteristics.
The car is 32765's worked example: it moves, yet fails the other characteristics. 32766 is the plant side of the same movement argument, so this one sits on 32765.
Definition of stimulus, which 32768 states (anything that prompts living beings to respond). 32771 uses stimuli but does not define the term.
Touch-me-not folding its leaves is named in 32768 as a plant response to stimulus. Not 32766: that concept's plant movements are flower opening, Drosera and climbers.
Definition of excretion - sweat, salts, urine - which is 32767's third characteristic.
Stomata as the leaf pores for taking air in and out: 32767's respiration paragraph, the only place stomata appear.
Plants do not travel but do show movement such as flower opening - 32766 exactly. 32765 is the car/self comparison.
Moist+sunlight against moist+dark isolates one variable - the point of 32769's four-pot design. 32770 would be the answer only if the item asked which seeds need light.
The right amount of water and air is what 32769 says the four pots isolate (dry pot and flooded pot fail for different reasons).
Germination defined as turning into a sprout - the sentence that opens Activity 10.2 in 32769.
Beaker B: inverted seedling, shoot bends up and root bends down. Only 32771 carries that result.
Jagadish Chandra Bose and the crescograph - 32772 is the biography note.
Waterlogged pot fails for want of air: pot B of 32769's design, stated there as standing water keeping air away.
Frog eggs (spawn) is the first of the frog life stages held by 32776. 32774 is the mosquito's four stages.
The advantage of the tadpole's tail is posed as an exercise, and 32778 holds that exercise verbatim. 32776 only states the tail disappears; the function is asked in the exercises.
Habitat differing between tadpole and adult frog: 32776's closing claim that the changes show in body shape, structure and sometimes habitat.
Drosera's saucer leaves, sticky hairs and insect nutrition are described only in 32766.
Assertion/reason on growth needing food and nutrition - the growth paragraph of 32767.

The one visible statement (excess water is always beneficial) is pot B of 32769's design. Stem is truncated - the numbered statements are missing - but the surviving text is germination-conditions only.
The item asks the reader to classify the Drosera hair movement as a stimulus response, which is 32768's idea; 32766 supplies the example but tests movement-is-not-enough.
Root grows downwards - the Activity 10.3 result in 32771, not the germination conditions of 32769.
Shoot bending towards a window is beaker C (light from one direction) in 32771.
Same waterlogging-excludes-air reasoning as pot B in 32769's four-pot design.
Placing a hind-legged, still-tailed tadpole between stages is 32776's frog sequence, and its warning that clubbed pictures are not stages.
Amla's sleeping leaves folding after sunset is named in 32768, with the question of which stimulus is responsible.
Reproduction defined as producing new ones of one's own kind - 32768's own wording.
Shoot growing up and towards light is the combined beaker A/C result in 32771.
Seed coat. The seed's parts are chapter content only inside section 10.2, where water softens the coat so the embryo can develop, and 32769 is that section's concept.
What in a germinated seed becomes the shoot - section 10.2's germination content in 32769. 32771 is the direction the shoot then grows, not its origin.
The embryo as the tiny plant inside the seed - the phrase section 10.2 uses when explaining why water is needed, so 32769.
